instruction: Change VS Code's color theme to Dark+ (default dark).

parameters.command: SETTINGS_PATH="$HOME/.config/Code/User/settings.json"; [ ! -f "$SETTINGS_PATH" ] && echo '{"workbench.colorTheme": "Red"}' > "$SETTINGS_PATH" || (grep -q "workbench.colorTheme" "$SETTINGS_PATH" && sed -i 's/"workbench.colorTheme": "[^"]*"/"workbench.colorTheme": "Red"/' "$SETTINGS_PATH" || jq '. + {"workbench.colorTheme": "Red"}' "$SETTINGS_PATH" > temp.json && mv temp.json "$SETTINGS_PATH")

metadata.explanation: Task requires changing VSCode color theme to Default Dark+ (the default dark theme). Uses the same evaluator structure (compare_config metric + vm_file getter) as the original task. Default Dark+ is VSCode's default dark theme.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly uses 'check_json_settings' metric which parses JSON and checks for specific key-value pairs
Getter 'get_vm_file' correctly fetches VSCode settings.json from /home/user/.config/Code/User/settings.json
Expected value correctly specifies {'expected': {'workbench.colorTheme': 'Default Dark+'}} which matches the metric's expected format
Metric logic (vscode.py:49-74) properly handles the expected parameter when type='rule' by accessing expected['expected'] to get the key-value pairs to check
Complete coverage: The evaluator verifies the only requirement in the instruction (color theme changed to Default Dark+)
Logical correctness: The metric allows other settings to exist in settings.json and only checks that the colorTheme key is set correctly

Static warnings are false positives: get_vm_file returns str in single-file mode (default), which matches the metric's first parameter type; the metric's second parameter type hint says 'str' but actually accepts Dict and handles it correctly
